title: Sell Mineral Rights in Rivesville, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Rivesville, WV
metaDescription: Rivesville, Marion County mineral owners: Monongahela River tracts, legacy Big Injun wells, and multi-generation heirship title checks.
heroLead: Rivesville sits along the Monongahela River in Marion County, on ground carrying decades of legacy gas production alongside newer Marcellus interest.
intro: This river community's surrounding acreage reflects Marion County's broader pattern: older Big Injun and Gordon sand wellbores from earlier drilling eras, family-held farm tracts split across generations, and periodic newer leasing tied to the county's Route 250 corridor development.

sections.heading: River-corridor production history
paragraphs: Rivesville-area tracts along the Monongahela have production histories reaching back through multiple drilling eras, meaning a single tract can carry both an old flat-rate lease on a legacy well and newer lease interest tied to horizontal development nearby. Sorting out which applies to your specific acreage takes an actual records check.

sections.heading: Family-held interests and heir shares
paragraphs: As with much of rural Marion County, Rivesville-area mineral ownership tends to be family-held and split across multiple heirs after generations of inheritance. A Marion County Courthouse records check in Fairmont establishes your current percentage before any sale or lease decision.

sections.heading: Where a Rivesville tract's mineral rights end and a neighbor's begin
paragraphs: River-corridor tracts near Rivesville sometimes have irregular boundaries tied to old river-lot surveys, which can make it less obvious than usual where one owner's mineral interest ends and a neighboring tract's begins, especially once a unit pools several of these irregular parcels together.
A title review working from the original survey descriptions, rather than a current tax map alone, is the reliable way to confirm your tract's actual boundaries before valuing the interest.

faqs.question: Does my Rivesville tract have more than one lease on it?
faqs.answer: It's possible if the tract has both a legacy shallow well and interest from newer Marcellus leasing. A title check clarifies which leases are currently in force.

faqs.question: Is my old Rivesville lease paying flat-rate?
faqs.answer: Check your division order's payment terms; flat-rate leases in this area can often be converted to a royalty basis under West Virginia law.

faqs.question: How do I confirm my share of a Rivesville family interest?
faqs.answer: A courthouse records check tracing the deed and will books establishes your current percentage.

faqs.question: How are irregular river-lot boundaries handled when a unit is formed near Rivesville?
faqs.answer: The operator's unit plat should reflect the actual surveyed boundaries; a title review confirms your tract's boundaries match what's been pooled.

faqs.question: Are Rivesville-area leases typically longer or shorter than newer Marcellus leases elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Older river-corridor leases sometimes carry primary terms and clauses that predate current standard forms, so comparing your specific lease language against modern conventions is worth doing.
